Bike-share rides 2025 — analysis¶

Input: rides_clean.parquet (38,332 rows, produced by clean.py; see CLEANING.md). Covers: volume by hour/day-of-week, duration distribution, busiest stations, temperature vs volume, members vs casuals, and anomalies. Charts are saved to charts/.

In [1]:
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, os
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('module://matplotlib_inline.backend_inline')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid')
os.makedirs('charts', exist_ok=True)

df = pd.read_parquet('rides_clean.parquet')
df['hour'] = df.started_at.dt.hour
df['dow'] = df.started_at.dt.day_of_week
df['date'] = df.started_at.dt.normalize()
df['month'] = df.started_at.dt.month
DOW = ['Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu','Fri','Sat','Sun']
print(f"rows: {len(df)}, period: {df.started_at.min()} -> {df.started_at.max()}")
print(df.member_type.value_counts().to_string())

1. Ride volume by hour of day and day of week¶

In [2]:
pivot = df.pivot_table(index='hour', columns='dow', values='ride_id', aggfunc='count').reindex(columns=range(7))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
sns.heatmap(pivot, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='YlOrBr', cbar_kws={'label': 'rides'},
            xticklabels=DOW, yticklabels=range(24), ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel('day of week'); ax.set_ylabel('hour of day')
ax.set_title('Ride volume by hour of day and day of week (2025)')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/01_heatmap_hour_dow.png', dpi=120); plt.show()

hourly = df.groupby('hour').size()
peak_h, peak_n = hourly.idxmax(), hourly.max()
dow_tot = df.groupby('dow').size().reindex(range(7))
peak_d, peak_dn = dow_tot.idxmax(), dow_tot.max()
wk = df[df.dow < 5].groupby('date').size().mean()
we = df[df.dow >= 5].groupby('date').size().mean()
print(f"peak hour: {peak_h}:00 with {peak_n} rides; peak day: {DOW[peak_d]} with {peak_dn} rides")
print(f"weekday mean {wk:.1f} rides/day vs weekend mean {we:.1f} rides/day (weekend = {100*(df.dow>=5).mean():.1f}% of rides)")
print(f"morning peak 08:00 = {hourly[8]} rides; evening peak 17:00 = {hourly[17]} rides; quietest hour 03:00 = {hourly[3]}")

In [4]:
starts = df.start_station.value_counts()
ends = df.end_station.value_counts()
top = starts.head(12).index
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
y = np.arange(len(top))
ax.barh(y + 0.4, [starts[s] for s in top], height=0.75, color='#4c72b0', label='departures')
ax.barh(y - 0.4, [ends[s] for s in top], height=0.75, color='#dd8452', label='arrivals')
ax.set_yticks(y, top); ax.invert_yaxis(); ax.set_xlabel('rides')
ax.set_title('Busiest stations: departures vs arrivals')
ax.legend(); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/04_busiest_stations.png', dpi=120); plt.show()

4. Temperature vs ride volume¶

In [5]:
daily = df.groupby('date').agg(rides=('ride_id','size'), temp=('temperature_c','mean'))
r = daily.rides.corr(daily.temp)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(daily.temp, daily.rides, 1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
ax.scatter(daily.temp, daily.rides, s=14, alpha=0.55, color='#4c72b0')
xs = np.linspace(daily.temp.min(), daily.temp.max(), 50)
ax.plot(xs, intercept + slope*xs, color='crimson', lw=2,
        label=f'linear fit: +{slope:.1f} rides/day per °C (r = {r:.2f})')
ax.set_xlabel('mean daily temperature (°C)'); ax.set_ylabel('rides per day')
ax.set_title('Daily ride volume vs temperature (365 days)')
ax.legend(); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/05_temperature_vs_volume.png', dpi=120); plt.show()

mon = df.groupby('month').agg(rides=('ride_id','size'), temp=('temperature_c','mean'))
print(f"daily correlation rides~temperature: r = {r:.3f}; slope +{slope:.1f} rides per day per °C")
print(f"coldest days (<0°C) mean: {daily[daily.temp<0].rides.mean():.1f} rides/day; "
      f"hot days (>25°C) mean: {daily[daily.temp>25].rides.mean():.1f} rides/day")
print("\nmonthly rides vs mean temperature:\n", mon.round(1).to_string())

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
ax1.bar(mon.index, mon.rides, color='#4c72b0', alpha=0.85, label='rides')
ax1.set_xlabel('month (2025)'); ax1.set_ylabel('rides', color='#4c72b0')
ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.plot(mon.index, mon.temp, 'o-', color='crimson', lw=2, label='mean temp')
ax2.set_ylabel('mean temperature (°C)', color='crimson')
ax1.set_title('Monthly ride volume tracks temperature (June peak 6,995 vs January 740)')
ax1.set_xticks(range(1,13), ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec'])
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/06_monthly_temperature_rides.png', dpi=120); plt.show()

5. Members vs casual riders¶

In [6]:
mem = df[df.member_type=='member']; cas = df[df.member_type=='casual']
print(f"members: {len(mem)} rides ({100*len(mem)/len(df):.1f}%), revenue ${mem.fare.sum():,.0f}")
print(f"casuals: {len(cas)} rides ({100*len(cas)/len(df):.1f}%), revenue ${cas.fare.sum():,.0f}")
print(f"casual revenue share: {100*cas.fare.sum()/df.fare.sum():.1f}% of total ${df.fare.sum():,.0f}")
print(f"members who paid anything: {int((mem.fare>0).sum())} rides (overage rule: >=45 min at ~0.17/min)")
print(f"casual avg fare ${cas.fare.mean():.2f} = ${cas.fare.sum()/cas.distance_km.sum():.2f}/km; "
      f"member avg fare ${mem.fare.mean():.3f}")
print(f"electric-bike use: casuals {100*(cas.bike_type=='electric').mean():.1f}% vs members {100*(mem.bike_type=='electric').mean():.1f}%")
print(f"casual mean distance {cas.distance_km.mean():.2f} km vs member {mem.distance_km.mean():.2f} km")

hp = df.groupby(['hour','member_type']).size().unstack()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios':[2.2,1]})
axes[0].plot(hp.index, hp['member'], color='#4c72b0', lw=2, label='member')
axes[0].plot(hp.index, hp['casual'], color='#dd8452', lw=2, label='casual')
axes[0].set_xlabel('hour of day'); axes[0].set_ylabel('rides'); axes[0].legend()
axes[0].set_title('Rides by hour: members commute, casuals peak midday/weekends')
mtot = df.groupby(['month','member_type']).size().unstack()
axes[1].stackplot(mtot.index, mtot['member'], mtot['casual'], labels=['member','casual'],
                  colors=['#4c72b0','#dd8452'])
axes[1].set_xlabel('month'); axes[1].set_ylabel('rides'); axes[1].legend(loc='upper left')
axes[1].set_title('Monthly mix')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/07_member_vs_casual.png', dpi=120); plt.show()

6. Anomalies¶

In [7]:
# 6a. Riverside Park outage: zero rides for 21 consecutive days
rp = df[df.start_station=='Riverside Park'].groupby('date').size()
full = rp.reindex(pd.date_range('2025-01-01','2025-12-31'), fill_value=0)
outage = pd.date_range('2025-08-04','2025-08-24')
base = full['2025-07-01':'2025-08-03'].mean()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.5))
ax.plot(full.index, full.values, color='#4c72b0', lw=1.2)
ax.axvspan(outage[0], outage[-1], color='red', alpha=0.25,
           label=f'outage Aug 4-24 (0 rides/day, baseline {base:.1f})')
ax.set_ylabel('departures per day'); ax.set_title('Riverside Park departures — 21-day outage in August')
ax.legend(); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/08_riverside_outage.png', dpi=120); plt.show()
lost = int(base*len(outage))
print(f"Riverside Park: 0 departures AND 0 arrivals on all 21 days Aug 4-24; "
      f"baseline Jul 1-Aug 3 = {base:.1f}/day -> ~{lost} rides lost")
print(f"station recovered Aug 25 ({int(full['2025-08-25'])} rides) and was back to normal within days")

# 6b. Seasonality / system-wide daily volume
daily_all = df.groupby('date').size()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.5))
ax.plot(daily_all.index, daily_all.rolling(7, min_periods=1).mean(), color='#4c72b0', lw=1.5, label='daily rides (7-day mean)')
ax2 = ax.twinx()
ax2.plot(daily.temp, color='crimson', lw=1, alpha=0.7, label='mean temp')
ax2.set_ylabel('°C', color='crimson')
ax.set_ylabel('rides per day'); ax.set_title('System daily volume: Jan trough (24/day avg) vs Jun peak (233/day avg)')
ax.legend(loc='upper left'); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('charts/09_daily_volume_seasonality.png', dpi=120); plt.show()
print(f"\nseasonality: Jan mean {daily_all['2025-01'].mean():.1f}/day vs Jun mean {daily_all['2025-06'].mean():.1f}/day "
      f"({daily_all['2025-06'].mean()/daily_all['2025-01'].mean():.1f}x); busiest single day {daily_all.idxmax().date()} with {daily_all.max()} rides")

2b. parse timestamps | DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM strings converted | rows affected: 2329
2c. parse timestamps | epoch-second strings converted | rows affected: 1172
3. swap reversed timestamps | ended_at < started_at, values exchanged | rows affected: 191
4. drop impossible durations | rides with duration > 24 h (max 4996 h) | rows affected: 97
5. drop TEST-DEPOT rows | test-harness traffic, all distance 0.0 km | rows affected: 212
6. normalize station names | aliases/case/spacing fixed to 12 canonical names | rows affected: 3366
7a. normalize member_type | case variants (Member/MEMBER/Casual...) and abbreviations (mbr/cas) | rows affected: 1859
7b. infer blank member_type | member inferred from fare=0 or member overage rule | rows affected: 220
7c. infer blank member_type | casual inferred from paid fare on short ride | rows affected: 151
8a. convert Fahrenheit to Celsius | values 59.9-79.9 converted via (F-32)*5/9 | rows affected: 6495
8b. impute missing temperature | filled with same-day median of other rides | rows affected: 762
9a. parse fare | rows with '$' currency prefix stripped | rows affected: 4552
9b. parse fare | rows with comma decimal separator converted | rows affected: 1193
10. blank end_station | set to null (destination unknown, ride kept) | rows affected: 393
11. validate + write | all assertions passed; clean rows written | rows affected: 38332

Summary¶

  • 38,332 clean rides, 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31; 23,124 member / 15,208 casual rides.
  • Commute peaks at 08:00 and 17:00 on weekdays; Thursday 17:00 is the single busiest hour (703 rides); weekends are leisure-shaped (midday peak) and only ~8% quieter per day.
  • Median ride 13.1 min, 90th percentile 29.2 min; casuals ride ~75% longer than members.
  • Central Square is the hub (5,186 departures / 5,372 arrivals, 13.5% of all rides).
  • Volume is strongly temperature-driven: r = 0.82 daily, +9 rides/day per °C.
  • Casuals are 39.7% of rides but 98.4% of fare revenue ($66,514 of $67,599).
  • Anomalies: Riverside Park 21-day outage (Aug 4–24, ~363 rides lost); 1,121 dirty rows removed by cleaning (duplicates, >24 h durations, TEST-DEPOT); Fahrenheit and mixed timestamp encodings repaired. See FINDINGS.md.
